chunks: From him, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Najrān, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from ʿĪṣ ibn al-Qāsim al-Bajalī, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a woman who begins menstruating in the month of Ramadan before the sun sets. He said: “She breaks her fast when she menstruates.”
And this report is not contradicted by that.
(1216) 39. What ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan narrated, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from his paternal uncle Yaʿqūb al-Aḥmar, from Abū Baṣīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

“If menstruation comes upon a woman in the month of Ramadan before noon, then she has latitude to eat and drink. But if it comes upon her after the sun has passed the meridian, then let her perform ghusl and count the fast of that day, so long as she has not eaten or drunk.”

So this report is an error from the narrator, because if the seeing of blood is what invalidates the fast, then it is not permissible for her to count that day. Rather, it is only recommended for her to refrain for the rest of the day as a matter of discipline if she sees blood after noon. The report that indicates this is:
(1217) 40. What ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl narrated, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a woman who sees blood in the early morning, or as the day rises, or at noon. He said: “She breaks her fast. And if that is after al-ʿaṣr or after noon, then let her continue upon her fast and make up that day.”

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: midday, when the sun passes the meridian
key_terms.تَقْضِ: she makes up the fast later
key_terms.تُفْطِرُ: she breaks her fast; her fasting ends
key_terms.تُمْسِكَ: she refrains from eating and drinking
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the month of Ramadan, the obligatory fasting month

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a woman begins menstruating during a fast in Ramadan?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the legal ruling for a woman who begins menstruating during a day of fasting in Ramadan. It states that the onset of menstruation invalidates the fast, while also preserving a scholarly note that refraining from eating for the rest of the day after noon may be recommended as a matter of discipline, though the day must still be made up.
